findings.msg: “The dative is ... used ... to say where something is” overgeneralizes the location rule. Location alone does not determine case: accusative prepositions retain their case even in descriptions of location. Specify that a location expressed with a two-way preposition takes the dative; other prepositions govern their own case.

The claim that nicht stands “just before” a final infinitive or separable particle is too restrictive. Other complements can intervene: Ich kann nicht nach Berlin kommen; Ich rufe nicht jeden Tag an. Say that nicht precedes the final verb component, with its precise position depending on what is negated.

“With feminine nouns and in the plural: mein + -e” omits the case restriction and conflicts with the dative forms taught elsewhere in this reference. Specify “in the nominative and accusative”; the dative requires meiner Mutter and meinen Eltern.
